label: text
text: A sense of typhoid fever (Chinese) is notified in the health return for Friday.

label: text
text: A report issued by the Glasgow Corporation Tramways shows — despite tradition — how easily the Scot and his money may be parted. During the year ended May 31 no fewer than 2,186 sums of money were found in the corporation's tramway-cars, "besides 918 parcels of clothing.

label: text
text: Despite the robbing at Messrs. Mackintosh's Ltd., reported elsewhere in this issue, the three days' sale, announced to commence there to-day, will be held in accordance with the original arrangements. The robbery will now be allowed to make the slightest different in connection with the sale of the prices.

label: text
text: The sharp shower which came down on Saturday afternoon did not more than spoil sport—it brought streams of water and several feet of mud across the road near the Nursing Home and the Cemetery, impeding traffic. Trum cars could not get round the Valley and came back the same way as they had been used to for a month until Monday last.

label: text
text: Sydney. — In view of the precarious position of many Tasmanian fruit growers as the result of the low prices prevailing in the London market, the Hobart Chamber of Commerce has appealed to the Federal Government to come to their relief. The Chamber of Commerce calls attention to "the extreme distress suffered by a large number of orchardists through the failure of the English market's in consequence of the general strike" and declares that many are penniless as a result of the failure and unable to prepare the soil for next season's crops.

label: text
text: Mr. Coates, the Prime Minister, in an address to the women's branch of the New Zealand Political Reform League, said that anyone knowing the active propaganda conducted at present, by people aiming at the disintegration of the Empire must realise how supremely important it is to maintain a Government in office which stands for King, Constitution, and country. His Government was endeavouring to inculcate among all citizens those basic principles of loyalty, patriotism, and respect for law and order without which no British people could really progress.

label: text
text: 'Mr. Bridgeman' (First, Lord of the Admiralty) stated in the House of Commons in reply to Major Glyn (U., Abingdon), that during present financial year twenty ships would be removed from the effective list of the Royal Navy. These vessels included Ajax, Thunderfer. King George V., and Agamemnon.

label: text
text: Sir Samuel Houru (Secretary of State for Air) has, by written answer, informed Colonel Day (Lab. Soc., Southwark, C.) that, approximately, 3,500 gallons of petrol were used by aeroplanes for the Air Force at the recent display at Hendon.

label: text
text: Dresden.—The German army appears to have obtained a new gas. Experiments were carried out recently near Dresden by an artillery regiment with this gas, which produces a dense fog over a large area. The thickness of the fog is such that it is impossible to see for more than a couple of yards. The new gas is stated to have no poisonous effects.

label: text
text: A hole about the size of a pin's head in lead casing deep in the ground below. Trafalgar Square, caused by vibration set up by the traffic overhead and a leaking water main, recently put out of service one of the largest telephone cables in London and rendered temporarily useless 240 telephones in the hotels, shops, and offices at Charing Cross. The exchanges affected were Gerrard and Regent.

label: text
text: Johannesburg. — Golf has been distinctly perilous at Beira lately owing to the presence of a lion and lioness, who made the links their home. Irate golfers objecting to this new hazard organised gun parties, and, accompanied by half the inhabitants of the town, armed with anything, had been scouring the links for several days. The animals were seen several times, but it was impossible to shoot at them for fear of hitting one of the hunters. Finally, a lucky shot on the part of the town's best golfers killed the lion, which was borne into the town amid great rejoicing. The lioness is still at large, and has taken up her residence in some bushes near the fourteenth hole.

label: text
text: Lady Chater, widow of Sir Paul Chater, of Hongkong, was among the passengers on board the Cunard liner "Mauretania," which arrived at Plymouth from New York on July 27.

label: text
text: A Civil List pension of £100 has been granted to Lady Dorothea, Hosie, in recognition of the public, literary, and scientific services rendered by her husband, the late Sir Alexander Hosie, M.A., LL.D., F.R.G.S.

label: text
text: A cablegram has been received in the Colony stating that Rt. Wor. Bro. J. Owen Hughes, Deputy District Grand Master of Hongkong and South China, E.C., has been appointed District Grand Master of the District of Hongkong and South China.

label: text
text: Lady Mabel Waldron Piggott has been granted a Civil List pension of £50 in recognition of her public services and the services rendered by her husband, the late Sir Francis Piggott, M.A., a former Chief Justice of Hongkong, especially in the study of international law.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOCIAL AND PERSONAL NEWS.

label: text
text: The King has given Mr. Norman Oswald Liddell, late Secretary and Commissioner General to the Shanghai Municipal Council, authority to wear the Insignia of the Fourth Class of the Order of the Excellent Crop, which decoration has been conferred on him by the President of the Republic of China in recognition of valuable services.

label: text
text: The Chinese Y.M.C.A. Division of the St. John's Ambulance Brigade is arranging a series of lectures for the benefit of the people in the more congested areas of the city. These lectures or "talks" will be directed towards the improvement in sanitary conditions. Dr. S. F. Li, a well-known local physician and surgeon-instructor of the Chinese Y.M.C.A. Division, has been helping the members of the brigade to prepare for their work. Dr. Li himself gave an instructive lecture on preventive measures against cholera at the Des Vaux Road Central Branch of the Chinese Y.M.C.A. on Thursday evening, when many local Chinese men were among those present.

label: text
text: Sir Basil Scott, of Tangier, Morocco, formerly Chief Justice of Bombay, left estate valued for the purposes of the English grant (net pers., £89,934) £100,396.

label: text
text: There is no foundation for the statement that the F. and O. and British India Companies are or have been interested in the proposed sale by the International Mercantile Marine of the White Star Line and its fleet.

label: text
text: "Mr. Hill, the South Australian Minister of Education, strongly favours a compulsory course of swimming," for school children, after passing a medical examination, as a definite part of the school curriculum. The Minister announced that the education vote this year would be approximately £1,000,000, but the Government was so anxious to advance the State school education that it was likely that even that amount would be exceeded.

label: text
text: A Ben Marshall oil painting of Mr. Fermor's Hounds at Tusmore, with a portrait of William Fermor, realised £4,200 at a sale at Croughton House, Brackley, Northamptonshire, the purchaser being Lord Woolavington.

label: text
text: Johannesburg. — A North-ern Transvaal farmer has had a thrilling experience. While taking a walk he came upon a huge lion having a sun bath. The beast joined a lioness 20 yards away, and their cub ran to the farmer, who hit it on the head with his stick. The lions then stamped a herd of cattle and killed several. Lions have been troublesome in the district.

label: text
text: Bisley, July 10.—A story that has sent a thrill through the camp, where all that it implies can best be appreciated, concerns the pluck of a Marleborough boy, who, although he was really too ill to be out of bed, refused to let his school down in the Ashburton Shield match. "Suffering considerable pain.. Cadet Robert Allen nevertheless insisted on shooting in the morning, when he put on 30 out of 35 at 200 yards. On the way to the camp he called for a drink of water at the North London Rifle Club. It was at once seen that he was ill, and he was offered a bed. But he refused to stay there, went on the range in the afternoon, and brought his aggregate to 61. Then he collapsed, and Dr. J. Elgood, the silver medallist of 1923, examined him and ordered his immediate removal to Guildford Hospital. There an operation for appendicitis was at once performed. A message from the hospital states that Allen is progressing favourably. It is considered that the knowledge that his shoot was completed and that he did not let his school down will materially aid his recovery.

label: text
text: Recently the foundation stone was laid of a Masonic Temple to be erected in Broad Street. Birmingham, at a cost of upwards of £60,000, as a memorial to the Freemasons of Warywickshire who fell in the war.

label: text
text: King Boris of Bulgaria is reported to have crossed the frontier into Jugo-Slavia with his sister, Princess Eudoxia, travelling by motor-car incognito. There is a possibility of his intention to abdicate. The sudden departure of the King from Bulgaria with Princess Eudoxia has excited great interest in political circles in Vienna, where it is connected with the growing difficulties of the Premier, M. Piaptsheff, and the strong opposition of the ex-Premier, M. Zankoff.—Exchange.

label: text
text: The Prince of Wales, wearing the Seaforth-Mackenzie tartan and Glengarry cap, inspected the 1st Seaforth Highlanders for the first time as their Colonel-in-Chief at Aldershot. As the Prince walked from his motor-car to the saluting base on the Salamanca parade ground his own standard was unfurled. After the inspection the battalion, led by Colonel Buchanan, raised their Glengarries aloft and gave three cheers for the Prince. An instance of the Prince's memory was later forthcoming. Mingling with the married families, who were in an enclosure on the fringe of the parade ground, the Prince addressed Mrs. Mackenzie, wife of Company-Sergeant-Major Mackenzie, and smilingly remarked, "I remember you in India. How long have you been home?" Mrs. Mackenzie told him, and added that she was pleased to be back in "old England" again.

label: text
text: Mr. Alexander Findlay Smith, J.P. F.R.G.S., of The Farm, The Peak, Hongkong, who died on January 10, aged 81, left personal property in England and Hongkong valued at £125,580, of which £6,750 is in England.

label: text
text: Captain George William Frederick Browne, R.N.R., late of the Penin-Silair and Oriental Steamship Company, who died on May 20, left estate of the gross value of £9,248, with net personality £9,115. He left the bulk of it to seamen's charities.

label: text
text: A Detroit message of August 22 reports: Walter Beach, pilot of a Wright travel aeroplane, was officially named as winner to-day after the second annual Ford reliability tour, scoring 4043.4 points. He wins the $7,000 Ford Cup, averaging 124 miles per hour for 6,252 miles.

label: text
text: Simla, August 13.—The Government of India anounces that it is giving executive effect to the Tariff Board's recommendation for the protection of the shipbuilding industry in India. The import duty will be either 10 per cent. ad valorem or Rs.35 per ton, whichever is higher, on fabricated steel parts for ships and other inland vessels.

label: text
text: Thirteen years ago a little girl named Munnings joined M. Serge Diaghileff's famous Russian Ballet company as a humble member of the corps de ballet now that little girl has an international reputation as Lydia Sokolova. Little Miss Munning, fair haired and blue eyed, came from Suffolk. The Munnings — Mr. A. J. Munnings' the painter, belongs to the family.

label: text
text:
London, August 12. — Lord Lloyd and his wife and son were involved in a motoring accident near Inverness. In order to avoid a pedestrian, Lord Lloyd swerved his car, which struck a wall and overturned on the occupants underneath. Sir John Harrington, who was passing, took them in his motor car to Inverness. In-
irmary. Although suffering from shock and cuts, they were able to go home.
